title: EPFO Death Claim: A Guide for Families to Claim PF, Pension Online
description: Families of deceased EPF members can claim Provident Fund (EPF), pension (EPS), and insurance (EDLI) benefits online. The online process requires the deceased.

faq.a: If there is no valid nomination, the benefits will be paid to the legal heirs of the deceased member, who will need to obtain a succession certificate or a letter of administration from a competent court.
Yes, a minor can claim benefits through their legal guardian. The guardian will need to submit a guardianship certificate along with other required documents.

faq.q: How long does the online claim process take?
faq.a: Typically, if all documents are in order and KYC is updated, online claims are settled within 20-30 days. Offline claims might take longer, usually 30-60 days.
The Employee Deposit Linked Insurance (EDLI) scheme provides a lump sum insurance payout to the nominee/legal heir of a deceased EPF member, with a maximum benefit of ₹7 lakhs.

faq.q: Is the EPF death claim taxable?
faq.a: No, the EPF amount received by the nominee or legal heir upon the death of the member is generally exempt from income tax, provided the member had completed at least five years of continuous service.

faq.q: What if the UAN is not activated?
faq.a: If the UAN is not activated, the family will likely have to resort to an offline claim process, as online claims heavily rely on an active UAN and linked Aadhaar.

faq.q: Can an NRI family member claim?
faq.a: Yes, an NRI family member can claim the benefits. They will need to provide their Indian bank account details (NRO/NRE account) and fulfil all other documentation requirements.
